question.:question/problem: Given the function $f(x,y)=3{x}^{2}+2x{y}^{2}-y$, find the equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(-1,1).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The equation of the tangent line to the level curve $f(x,y)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(x,y)=(-1,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(3{x}^{2}+2x{y}^{2}-y)\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(3{x}^{2}+2x{y}^{2}-y)\,j \\  & =(6x+2{y}^{2})\text{ }i+(4xy-1)\text{ }j \\ ∇\,f(-1,1) & =(6(-1)+2(1)^{2})\,i+(4(-1)(1)-1)\,j \\  & =-4\,i-5\,j \\  & =⟨-4,-5⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the Cartesian equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be written as:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(-1,1)\cdot ⟨x+1,\,y-1⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨-4,-5⟩\cdot ⟨x+1,\,y-1⟩ & =0\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Given the function $f(x,y)=\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}^{2})-3{y}^{3}$, find the equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(\sqrt{\pi },2).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The equation of the tangent line to the level curve $f(x,y)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(x,y)=(\sqrt{\pi },2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}^{2})-3{y}^{3})\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}^{2})-3{y}^{3})\,j \\  & =-2x\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}^{2})\,i-9{y}^{2}\,j \\ ∇\,f(\sqrt{\pi },2) & =-2\sqrt{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡((\sqrt{\pi })^{2})i-9(2)^{2}\,j \\  & =-2\sqrt{\pi }\cdot 0\,i-36\,j \\  & =-36\,j \\  & =⟨0,-36⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the Cartesian equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be written as:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(\sqrt{\pi },2)\cdot ⟨x-\sqrt{\pi },\,y-2⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨0,-36⟩\cdot ⟨x-\sqrt{\pi },\,y-2⟩ & =0\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Given the function $f(x,y)=\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1),$ find the equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(-1,0).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The equation of the tangent line to the level curve $f(x,y)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(x,y)=(-1,0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1))\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1))\,j \\  & =\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1}\,i+\frac{2y}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1}\,j \\ ∇f(-1,0) & =\frac{2(-1)}{(-1)^{2}+{0}^{2}+1}\,i+\frac{2(0)}{(-1)^{2}+{0}^{2}+1}\,j \\  & =(-1)i+0\,j \\  & =⟨-1,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the Cartesian equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(-1,0)\cdot ⟨x-(-1),\,y-0⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨-1,0⟩\cdot ⟨x+1,\,y⟩ & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Given the function $f(x,y)={x}^{2}-4xy+5{y}^{2}$ find the equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(-1,-1).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The equation of the tangent line to the level curve $f(x,y)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(x,y)=(-1,-1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}-4xy+5{y}^{2})\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}-4xy+5{y}^{2})\,j \\  & =(2x-4y)\,i+(10y-4x)\,j \\ ∇f(-1,-1) & =(2(-1)-4(-1))\,i+(10(-1)-4(-1))\,j \\  & =2\,i-6\,j \\  & =⟨2,-6⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the Cartesian equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(-1,-1)\cdot ⟨x-(-1),\,y-(-1)⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨2,-6⟩\cdot ⟨x+1,\,y+1⟩ & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Given the function $f(x,y)={x}^{2}{y}^{2}+xy$, find the equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(1,2).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The equation of the tangent line to the level curve $f(x,y)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be expressed as 

$$

$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(x,y)=(1,2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}{y}^{2}+xy)\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}{y}^{2}+xy)\,j \\  & =(2x{y}^{2}+y)\,i+(2y{x}^{2}+x)\,j \\ ∇\,f(1,2) & =(2(1)(2)^{2}+(2))\,i+(2(2)(1)^{2}+(1))\,j \\  & =10\,i+5\,j \\  & =⟨10,5⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the Cartesian equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be written as:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(1,2)\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-2⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨10,5⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-2⟩ & =0\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Given the function $f(x,y)=x{y}^{2}-x+y,$ find the equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(1,-1).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The equation of the tangent line to the level curve $f(x,y)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(x,y)=(1,-1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x{y}^{2}-x+y)\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(x{y}^{2}-x+y)\,j \\  & =({y}^{2}-1)\text{ }i+(2xy+1)\text{ }j \\ ∇f(1,-1) & =((-1)^{2}-1)\,i+(2(1)(-1)+1)\,j \\  & =0\,i-j \\  & =⟨0,-1⟩\end{aligned}

Now, the Cartesian equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(1,-1)\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-(-1)⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨0,-1⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y+1⟩ & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

question.:question/problem: Given the function $f(x,y)=\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}^{2}-y)$ find the equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(0,\pi ).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The equation of the tangent line to the level curve $f(x,y)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(x,y)=(0,\pi ):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}^{2}-y))\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}^{2}-y))\,j \\  & =2x\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}^{2}-y)\,i-\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}^{2}-y)\,j \\ ∇f(0,\pi ) & =2(0)\operatorname{cos}⁡({0}^{2}-\pi )\,i-\operatorname{cos}⁡({0}^{2}-\pi )\,j \\  & =0\,i+j \\  & =⟨0,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the Cartesian equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(0,\pi )\cdot ⟨x-0,\,y-\pi ⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨0,1⟩\cdot ⟨x,\,y-\pi ⟩ & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

The equation of the tangent line to the level curve $f(x,y)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$

$$

question.:question/problem: Given the function $f(x,y)={x}^{2}y+5xy-5x{y}^{2}$, find the equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(3,2).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The equation of the tangent line to the level curve $f(x,y)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(x,y)=(3,2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}y+5xy-5x{y}^{2})i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}y+5xy-5x{y}^{2})j \\  & =(2xy+5y-5{y}^{2})i+({x}^{2}+5x-10xy)j \\ ∇\,f(3,2) & =(2(3)(2)+5(2)-5(2)^{2})i+((3)^{2}+5(3)-10(3)(2))j \\  & =2\,i-36\,j \\  & =⟨2,-36⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the Cartesian equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be written as:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(3,2)\cdot ⟨x-3,\,y-2⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨2,-36⟩\cdot ⟨x-3,\,y-2⟩ & =0\end{aligned}
$$
